Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that this can be a really challenging and overwhelming time for new mothers, and I'm here to support you in any way I can.

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand how you're feeling and to identify any potential concerns that may be affecting your postpartum experience. The EPDS is a tool that helps us screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a really valuable way for us to get a sense of how you're doing and whether there's anything we can do to support you.

Please know that everything we discuss today is completely confidential, and I'm here to create a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. I want you to feel comfortable and heard, and I'm committed to providing you with the care and support you need during this time.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better sense of your emotional well-being over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and comfortable as possible.

So, let's get started. Here's my first question: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

(sighing) Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still try to enjoy the little things, like my baby's smile or a funny video, but it's just not the same. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time. I'm so tired all the time, and worrying about the baby's health and safety is always on my mind. It's hard to find the energy to laugh or feel carefree when I'm constantly thinking about whether I'm doing everything right as a mom. Sometimes, I do catch myself smiling or laughing at something, but it's not as frequent as it used to be. (pausing, looking down) I just feel really overwhelmed and sad a lot of the time, and it's hard to shake that off.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking head) No, not really. Like I said, it's just not the same as it used to be. I feel like I've lost interest in a lot of things that used to make me happy. Even when I do try to watch a funny movie or TV show, I just can't seem to fully enjoy it. My mind starts wandering to all the things I need to do for the baby, or worrying about whether I'm doing a good job as a mom. It's hard to explain, but it's like the happiness and laughter just aren't as accessible to me right now. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to be happy, but deep down, I'm really struggling.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(sighing) Not really. To be honest, I've been feeling really meh about most things lately. I used to love planning outings or trying new restaurants, but now I just feel overwhelmed by the thought of leaving the house with the baby. Even things that I used to enjoy, like reading or taking a bath, just don't seem as appealing to me anymore. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and the house, but I'm not really looking forward to anything. (pausing, looking down) Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, but then I'll just feel guilty for wanting to take time for myself, or I'll worry that I'm not doing enough for the baby. It's hard to explain, but it's like I've just lost my sense of purpose and joy in things. (voice cracking) It's really scary to feel like this, because I don't know how to get back to being myself.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, tears welling up in eyes) Oh, yeah... all the time. I feel like I'm just not doing enough, or that I'm not doing things right. If the baby cries, I think it's because I'm not feeding her enough, or that I'm not burping her right. If she spits up, I think it's because I'm not holding her at the right angle. It's like, no matter what happens, I always find a way to blame myself. (voice shaking) And it's not just with the baby, it's with everything. If the house is a mess, I feel like it's because I'm a bad mom and I'm not keeping up. If my partner is stressed, I feel like it's because I'm not supporting them enough. (wiping away tears) It's just this constant feeling of guilt and inadequacy, like I'm just not good enough at any of this. (sighing) It's really hard to shake off, and it's always there, lurking in the back of my mind.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, all the time. I worry about everything. I worry that the baby is going to get sick, or that I'm not feeding her enough, or that I'm not doing enough to stimulate her development. I worry that I'm not a good mom, that I'm not doing things right. (voice rising) I worry about SIDS, and about her rolling over and falling off the bed, and about her getting hurt. I worry about everything, all the time. (taking a deep breath) Even when my partner tries to reassure me, or when the pediatrician tells me that everything is fine, I just can't seem to shake off the feeling of worry. It's like, my mind is always racing, always thinking of all the worst-case scenarios. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for something bad to happen, like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop. It's exhausting, and it's hard to explain, but it's just this constant feeling of anxiety and worry that I just can't seem to escape.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, looking anxious) Yes, that happens to me too. Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. (taking a deep breath) It's like, my mind will start racing and I'll think about all the things that could go wrong, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of fear. (looking down, voice shaking) It's hard to explain, but it's like, I'll be fine one minute, and then the next minute I'll just feel like I'm losing control. (pausing, collecting thoughts) Sometimes it's triggered by something, like a loud noise or a sudden movement, but other times it just comes out of nowhere. (looking up, eyes wide with fear) And it's so scary, because I don't know what's happening or how to make it stop. (voice barely above a whisper) I just feel like I'm losing my grip on reality, and it's terrifying.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, feeling overwhelmed) Yes, that's exactly how I feel. Like, everything is just piling up on me and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner and friend... it's all just so much. (sighing) And I feel like I'm not doing any of it well. I'm just barely keeping my head above water, you know? (looking down, feeling defeated) Some days, it feels like everything is just too much for me to handle. I'll be trying to get the baby to sleep, and the laundry is piling up, and the dishes are stacked up in the sink... and I just feel like I'm drowning in all of it. (voice cracking) I'll try to make a to-do list, or prioritize things, but it always seems like there's just too much to do. And then I feel guilty for not being able to do it all, for not being a better mom or partner or person. (shaking head) It's just... it's all so overwhelming.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a lump form in throat) Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. Even when she's sleeping, I'll lie awake for hours, just thinking about everything that's been stressing me out. (sighing) My mind will start racing, and I'll think about all the things I need to do, or all the things I'm worried about, and I just can't seem to turn it off. (looking down, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) And then I'll start to feel really sad and overwhelmed, and I'll just lie there, feeling hopeless. (voice cracking) Some nights, I'll cry myself to sleep, just feeling like I'm not doing anything right, and that I'm just a failure as a mom. (wiping away tears) It's hard to explain, but it's like, my brain just won't shut off, and I'm stuck in this cycle of worry and sadness, and I don't know how to escape it. (pausing, taking a deep breath) And then, of course, I'll feel guilty for not being able to sleep, because I know I need rest to take care of the baby, and it just feels like this vicious cycle that I don't know how to break.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, feeling a wave of emotions) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really living. (sighing) It's hard to explain, but it's like, I'll be holding the baby, and I'll look at her, and I'll feel this overwhelming sense of love for her, but at the same time, I'll feel this deep sadness and emptiness. (looking down, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) It's like, I'm supposed to be happy, I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my new baby, but instead, I just feel lost and alone. (voice cracking) I'll be doing everyday tasks, like feeding her or changing her diaper, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me, and I'll start to cry. (wiping away tears) It's like, I'm grieving the person I used to be, and the life I used to have, and I don't know how to come to terms with this new reality. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Some days, it feels like the sadness is just suffocating me, and I don't know how to escape it. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) I just feel like I'm not myself anymore, and I don't know how to get back to being me.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears streaming down face) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, the smallest thing will set me off, and I'll just break down in tears. (sobbing) I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, or just sitting there, and suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness and I'll start to cry. (wiping away tears) It's like, I'm just so exhausted, and so overwhelmed, and so worried, and it all just comes out in tears. (sniffling) Sometimes I'll cry for hours, just sitting there, feeling like I'm all alone, and like I'm not doing anything right. (looking down, feeling ashamed) I'll try to hide it from my partner, or from my family, but it's hard to pretend like everything is okay when it's not. (voice cracking) I just feel like I'm failing, like I'm not good enough, and it's all just too much for me to handle. (sobbing uncontrollably) I just wish someone could tell me that I'm doing okay, that I'm not alone, and that everything is going to be alright. (between sobs) I just wish I could feel happy again, and not just be consumed by this sadness and worry all the time.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(shaking head) No, that's not something I've thought about. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad, and like I don't know how to make it all better, but harming myself has never crossed my mind. (looking down, feeling a sense of relief) I think that's because, even though things feel really tough right now, I know that I have people who care about me, and who would be devastated if anything happened to me. (pausing, thinking about loved ones) My partner, my family, my friends... they all love me, and they all want to help me through this. (looking up, feeling a sense of hope) And I know that, no matter how hard things get, I can always reach out to them for support. (smiling slightly) Plus, I have my baby to think about, and I know that I need to be here for her, to take care of her and to watch her grow. (nodding) So, no, harming myself has never been an option for me. I just need to find ways to manage my feelings, and to get through this tough time.

The patient presents with a range of emotional and behavioral concerns that suggest a potential risk for postpartum depression or anxiety, including persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, and enjoyment in activities, difficulty coping with daily responsibilities, and excessive guilt and self-blame regarding her role as a mother. The patient also reports anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed, as well as sleep difficulties linked to her mood, with frequent crying spells and emotions ranging from sadness to frustration.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 27, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>The patient states they can't seem to fully enjoy things that used to make them happy, and that happiness and laughter aren't accessible to them, which aligns with the 'Not at all' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Hardly at all' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes frequent and intense feelings of panic and fear, often without a clear trigger, and experiences physical symptoms such as a racing heart and feeling like they're going to pass out, indicating a high level of distress.</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates that they have been experiencing difficulty sleeping due to feelings of unhappiness, stress, and worry, which aligns with the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>Patient's response indicates feeling sad and miserable most of the time, describing it as overwhelming and suffocating, and feeling like they're not themselves anymore.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates that they have been crying a lot lately, even over small things, and that it happens frequently, such as when feeding or changing the baby, which suggests that they have been unhappy and crying most of the time.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's EPDS score of 27 indicates a high risk for postpartum depression, with symptoms including <sym>persistent sadness</sym>, <sym>loss of pleasure</sym>, <sym>excessive guilt</sym>, <sym>anxiety</sym>, <sym>panic</sym>, and <sym>sleep difficulties</sym>. These symptoms are consistent with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The patient's reports of feeling overwhelmed, anxious, and guilty also suggest a potential risk for <med>anxiety disorders</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage sleep hygiene practices, such as establishing a consistent sleep schedule and creating a relaxing bedtime routine
3. Support patient in developing coping strategies for managing anxiety and guilt, such as deep breathing exercises, mindfulness, or journaling
4. Provide patient with resources for <med>postpartum support groups</med> and online forums
5. Recommend patient keep a mood journal to track symptoms and identify patterns
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
